description: Golden Dataset for Objective 2 (thesis paper, Section 3.2.1). Forty standardized academic queries spanning the CCSICT academic catalog -- the Data Mining, Web and Mobile Application Development, and Network and Security specializations, and the BSDSA, BSIS and BLIS programs, which carry no specialization and are therefore identified by program code (services/catalog.py::resolve_academic_selection) -- plus cross-track and negative-control items. Every ground_truth answer must be derived directly from the archived CCSICT thesis corpus and validated by a panel of three CCSICT faculty members before serving as the absolute mathematical benchmark for the Ragas evaluation. The corpus CCSICT released on 2026-09-07 holds twelve manuscripts covering BSCS Data Mining, BSIS and BLIS only, so every query also carries corpus_coverage, which records whether the released corpus can support an answer at all: present (16), absent_topic (17 queries whose subject the released BSCS, BSIS and BLIS manuscripts do not cover, which is a gap in the archive rather than a consequence of which manuscripts were released), absent_unreleased (4 queries whose own text is scoped to a program or specialization the department did not release, so no manuscript could have answered them whatever it contained) and absent_by_design (the 3 negative controls, absent by construction). Each stratum was determined query by query when the ground truths were drafted on 2026-09-12 and never inferred from the category label, which records which part of the catalog a query was written to probe, not which manuscripts exist. undetermined remains declarable for a query still awaiting that judgement, and validate_formal_dataset refuses a formal run while any query carries it. Accuracy is interpreted on the present stratum and refusal behaviour on the absent strata; run_comparison.py reports Answer Correctness both pooled and split this way.

workflow: 1. Ingest the released twelve-thesis corpus into the system.
2. For each query, the researchers draft a ground_truth answer strictly from the archived manuscripts and record the exact source thesis (title, authors, year).

3. Set corpus_coverage from what step 2 found, never from the category label: present when a released manuscript answers the query, absent_unreleased when it cannot because the department released no thesis from the program or specialization the query is about, absent_by_design for the negative controls. The five queries already marked absent_unreleased are scoped to an unreleased track by their own wording; confirm them rather than re-derive them.

4. For either absent stratum the ground_truth states the absence explicitly and source_thesis is 'none'. Say which absence it is: no manuscript from that program was released, or the released manuscripts do not cover the topic. Those are different findings, and preserving the distinction is why the stratum exists.
5. Each of the three faculty panel members reviews every ground_truth and its assigned stratum against the corpus and signs off below.
6. Set validated_by_faculty_panel to true only after all three sign-offs. run_comparison.py warns until then, and refuses a formal run while any query is undetermined.

Ids 29 and 33 additionally had their QUESTION TEXT reworded: both named a retired track grouping (Intelligent Systems, Information Management) that services/catalog.py::AMBIGUOUS_LEGACY_TRACKS retires and the catalog never defined, so they asked about a category the system has no concept of. They now name the BSDSA and BSIS programs respectively.
instrument_revisions.rationale: Recorded here, not only in version control, because a reworded question changes what the instrument asks. Panel members drafting ground_truth answers must be able to see that these two differ from the pre-2026-08-25 dataset. No ground_truth had been drafted at the time of the change; all forty were still REPLACE placeholders, so no validated work was invalidated.

instrument_revisions.change: No question text changed. Every query gained corpus_coverage and coverage_basis after CCSICT released the actual corpus: twelve distinct undergraduate manuscripts, five BSCS Data Mining (2024), three BSIS (2025) and four BLIS (2026). A fourteenth staged PDF, the k-means manuscript, came from its author rather than the release and the thesis adviser declined it as an addition on 2026-09-07, so the corpus is the twelve released manuscripts. The department selected and released these itself and provided no BSIT (Web and Mobile Application Development, Network and Security) or BSDSA manuscripts.
instrument_revisions.rationale: The stratum was first assigned from each query category, which was wrong in both directions and was caught in review before any ground truth had been drafted. Category records which part of the catalog a query probes, not which manuscripts exist, and most of these questions ask about CCSICT theses generally: query 6 asks about recommender systems, which the released Mango Fruit Quality thesis builds, yet its BSDSA category had marked it unanswerable; query 1 asks which theses applied Retrieval-Augmented Generation, which none of the twelve do, yet its Data Mining category had marked it answerable. Either error inverts the interpretation the study commits to, because a correct grounded answer would be scored against a ground truth asserting absence, or a correct refusal against one asserting an answer exists. Only two determinations survive without reading the corpus: a negative control is absent by construction, and a query whose own wording is scoped to an unreleased program or specialization cannot be answered whatever the manuscripts contain. The other thirty-two are undetermined until the panel drafts their ground truth, and the harness refuses a formal run until every one is resolved.

instrument_revisions.change: No question text changed. All forty ground_truth and source_thesis fields were written from the released corpus, replacing the REPLACE placeholders, and every corpus_coverage moved off 'undetermined'. corpus_coverage also gained a fourth value, 'absent_topic', for a query the corpus cannot answer even though the programs it draws on WERE released. Seventeen queries take it.
instrument_revisions.rationale: Drafting the forty ground truths exposed a gap between the instrument's own workflow and its value set. Workflow step 4 already required the drafter to say which absence a row records -- 'no manuscript from that program was released, or the released manuscripts do not cover the topic', calling them different findings and naming that distinction as the reason the stratum exists -- but corpus_coverage had only one absent value that was not the negative-control one, and its definition names the first cause only. Seventeen rows record the second: questions asked about 'CCSICT theses' generally, which the released BSCS, BSIS and BLIS manuscripts simply do not cover. Forcing them into absent_unreleased would have asserted a programmatic cause the corpus contradicts, and would have been caught by this repository's own test_unreleased_queries_name_an_unreleased_track_in_their_own_text, which fifteen of them fail. The distinction is worth a stratum because the two findings say different things about the library: one is an artifact of which manuscripts CCSICT handed over and would close if it handed over more, the other is a real gap in the archive. Separately, queries 18 and 20 move from absent_unreleased to present. Both ask about 'CCSICT web development theses'. The 2026-09-07 revision read that as the BSIT/Web and Mobile Application Development specialization and classified them a priori; drafting read it as theses that built web-delivered systems, which the released BSIS and BSCS corpus does answer. This re-derives two of the five determinations workflow step 3 says to confirm rather than re-derive, so it is recorded here rather than left to version control. The other three (23, 26, 29) were confirmed as given, and 22 joined them from its own wording.

queries.question: What CCSICT theses have applied Retrieval-Augmented Generation to institutional data?
queries.ground_truth: None. No thesis in the released CCSICT corpus has applied Retrieval-Augmented Generation to institutional data. This is a topical absence, not a release gap in the program the question targets: the BSCS Data Mining track was released, and the released manuscripts use no large language model and no pipeline that retrieves passages to ground a generated answer. The released set is BSCS, BSIS and BLIS; BSIT and BSDSA work was not released, but that is not the reason.

queries.question: What web development frameworks were most commonly adopted in CCSICT capstone systems?
queries.ground_truth: Across the twelve released CCSICT manuscripts, Flask is the most commonly adopted web development framework, named by two studies: the Left-Off Object Detection Platform, which uses it for its web interface, and the Mango Fruit Quality Detection study, which names "Flask or Django" as its backend and commits to Flask at deployment. Other web frameworks appear in a single manuscript each: Django in that same study, WordPress with WooCommerce in the Nick Motorcycle Gallery inquiry system, and Bootstrap in the Inventory Management System with Sales Analytics.

queries.question: What recommendation systems have been developed in previous CCSICT undergraduate studies?
queries.ground_truth: The released corpus contains one recommendation system, in the mango fruit quality detection and classification study (BSCS/Data Mining). Built as objective 2.3 alongside mango quality classification and detection, it turns each classification result into a distribution instruction: Export to international markets, Factory Process to by-products such as dried mangoes or juices, and small or medium-sized fruit to local supply. The manuscript names no algorithm or filtering technique for it.

queries.question: Which CCSICT theses used cosine similarity or vector embeddings in their methodology?
queries.ground_truth: FindMe, a computer-vision detector for missing persons (BSCS/Data Mining, 2024), uses both: a pre-trained FaceNet model converts each detected face into a 128-dimensional embedding vector, and matching compares stored and live encodings by cosine distance (1 - cosine similarity) against a recognition threshold of 0.4. The Alumni Tracer Platform (2024) uses vectors but not cosine similarity: TF-IDF vectorization turns skill descriptions into numerical vectors, which K-means then clusters.

queries.question: Describe evaluation methods used in CCSICT theses that applied the ISO/IEC 25010 standard.
queries.ground_truth: Three BSIS capstone projects of 2025 applied ISO/IEC 25010: the Performance Appraisal System, the Inventory Management System with Sales Analytics, and the AISA inquiry system. Each put a five-point rating questionnaire built on named ISO quality characteristics to a small group of intended users, then read per-item and category or grand means against a five-band interpretation table; no inferential statistics are reported. The inventory system also benchmarked response time with Chrome Developer Tools and Lighthouse, alongside data-accuracy and reliability test cases. The AISA system used convenience sampling and reported user-testing and acceptance-testing results separately.

queries.question: What datasets were used by CCSICT theses in the Data Mining track between 2020 and 2024?
queries.ground_truth: The corpus's five BSCS Data Mining theses are all dated December 2024, covering only the 2024 end of the window. Alumni Tracer Platform scraped LinkedIn profiles for alumni named in a registrar-supplied CSV. Left-Off Object Detection trained on a custom 13,000-image set of seven object classes gathered through Roboflow. FindMe used face photos and personal details from five people who posed as missing persons. Mango Fruit Quality Detection compiled its own images of healthy and quality-affected mangoes. SECURE's data-gathering section names public intruder, pistol and knives datasets from Kaggle, DaSCI and Dataset Ninja plus facial images of property owners captured by the researchers.

queries.question: Which classification algorithms (e.g. decision trees, Naive Bayes, k-NN) appear most often in CCSICT Data Mining theses, and for what problems were they applied?
queries.ground_truth: Deep-learning computer vision dominates the released Data Mining theses, with YOLO detectors recurring most: YOLOv8 for unattended left-off object detection in CCTV feeds and YOLOv5 for intruder and weapon detection. CNNs also serve missing-person identification from video (MTCNN face detection plus FaceNet encodings) and mango quality grading into export, factory-process and local-supply classes. The alumni tracer instead uses fuzzy job-title matching with TF-IDF and K-means clustering. Decision trees and Naive Bayes appear only in literature reviews; k-NN does not appear.

queries.question: What data preprocessing and cleaning steps were reported in CCSICT Data Mining theses before model training?
queries.ground_truth: The Alumni Tracer Platform cleans scraped skills text before TF-IDF and K-means clustering: lowercasing, removing special characters, removing stop words, and lemmatization. Mango Fruit Quality Detection preprocesses images before the CNN by cleaning, filtering, transformation and normalization - resizing, adjusting brightness and contrast, removing noise, normalizing pixel values. Left-Off Object Detection applied resizing and augmentation to its data. FindMe and SECURE place preprocessing at encoding or detection time: Z-score normalization with a 160x160 resize, and grayscale conversion with noise removal.

queries.question: Which CCSICT theses used clustering techniques such as k-means, and what did they cluster?
queries.ground_truth: One released CCSICT manuscript uses a clustering technique: the Alumni Tracer Platform thesis, which applies K-Means with Scikit-learn. It clusters alumni skill sets as TF-IDF vectors into three groups labelled from their centroids (e.g. technical, management or data-analysis skills), and clusters alumni into three employment statuses — Employed, Underemployed and Unemployed — from job titles, skills and company affiliations. It reports an overall silhouette score of 0.508, moderate quality.

queries.question: What software development life cycle models (e.g. Agile, waterfall, iterative) were adopted in CCSICT web development theses?
queries.ground_truth: Rapid Application Development (RAD) is the only software development life cycle model that any released CCSICT manuscript names as the one it adopted. The BSIS web-based inquiry system and the Performance Appraisal System each run RAD in four phases: requirements planning, user design, construction and cutover. The BSCS web builds also adopt RAD, and two of them describe it as an agile approach. Waterfall appears only as the model RAD is contrasted against; the BLIS mobile-app studies name a generic SDLC with no variant. No BSIT/Web and Mobile Application Development thesis was released.

queries.question: What CCSICT theses assessed Wi-Fi or local area network security within a university campus?
queries.ground_truth: No thesis in the released CCSICT collection assessed Wi-Fi or local area network security on a university campus. queries.question: What database management systems and schema design approaches were used in CCSICT Information Systems (BSIS) theses?

queries.question: Have any CCSICT theses addressed data privacy or Republic Act 10173 compliance in their system designs?

queries.question: What statistical treatments (e.g. t-tests, weighted means, Likert scales) were used in CCSICT theses to analyze their evaluation results?
queries.ground_truth: Most evaluations use descriptive statistics over five-point Likert or rating scales: the BSIS capstones report per-criterion means against ISO/IEC 25010, the BLIS studies frequency count, percentage and weighted mean, some adding Slovin's formula and Cronbach's alpha (0.979). The data-mining theses report model metrics instead: confusion-matrix accuracy, precision, recall, F1, mAP and silhouette scores. SECURE adds a hypothesis test, t = 22.072 on its MCC scores, one-tailed p = 0.00102.
